companyDescription: Semiconductor + software · Custom AI chips (XPU) for Google/Meta + networking silicon for data centers
priceNote: Jun 22 live · -3.45% · Ex-dividend day ($2.60) + Google chip delay fears — JPMorgan: 'ignore the noise', PT $580
summary: Broadcom is the stealth AI winner — custom AI chips (XPUs) for Google, Meta, Apple plus AI networking (Ethernet switching) are compounding into a $60B+ AI revenue business by 2027. VMware integration now cash-flow positive ahead of schedule, and the recurring software revenue transforms the P&L permanently. New: Apollo/Blackstone $35B AI platform deal (Jun 9) validates AVGO as AI infrastructure backbone.

catalysts.name: Custom AI XPU Business
catalysts.description: Google TPUs, Meta MTIA, Apple neural engine — AVGO designs them all. TAM expanding to $60-90B by 2027 per management guidance.

catalysts.name: Apollo/Blackstone $35B AI Platform
catalysts.description: Broadcom, Apollo, and Blackstone launched a $35B AI infrastructure platform (Jun 9) — backs 20+ GW of AI deployment using AVGO chips. Validates AVGO as the infrastructure layer.

catalysts.name: VMware Integration Ahead of Schedule
catalysts.description: Subscription transition completed. $8.5B annual recurring revenue locked. EBITDA margin expanding to 65%+.

risks: Customer concentration: Google + Meta = ~40% of AI chip revenue
Google chip program delay fears — JPMorgan says 'ignore the noise' but risk real
AMD and Marvell competing for custom silicon wins
VMware enterprise churn if pricing pushes customers to alternatives
Debt load from VMware acquisition (~$70B) limits buyback flexibility
US-China trade restrictions could hit legacy semiconductor revenue

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Rate cuts reduce VMware debt servicing costs — meaningful for FCF expansion
macroRisk.inflationNote: Software-heavy mix insulates from materials inflation; semiconductor margins stable
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Tech sector broadly benefits from rate cuts; AVGO software revenue is recession-resilient
macroRisk.summary: Low macro sensitivity. AI custom silicon + VMware ARR = durable revenue regardless of rates.

entryStrategy.verdict: Core holding — BUY on any dip into $380–390. Today's -3.45% = ex-div ($2.60) + noise. AI XPU + VMware ARR is a rare quality+growth combo.

catalystSpot.preRunup: AVGO typically runs +5–12% in the 1–2 weeks before earnings, especially when AI chip design win news leaks (Apple, Google, Meta). Enter before earnings to capture the run-up rather than waiting for announcement day.

earningsHistory.note: 3 AI customers revealed, $60–90B TAM by 2027 — crossed $1T (outlier)
Beat + strong Q2 guide (~+16% after-hours, ~+8% next session)
Beat but FY27 AI target left unchanged → sell-the-news
Beat, AI chip sales to double — mostly priced in
Beat + raise, modest reaction at elevated valuation
Beat but FY27 AI target again unchanged → re-rate at premium

postWin.note: 7-quarter sample (FY24–FY26): 5 positive reactions averaging ~+10%. Median is closer to +5–8% — the +24% (Dec 2024 TAM reveal) is the outlier, not the base case. Big moves now require a genuinely new datapoint (new customer / TAM raise), not just a beat.

postLose.note: Recent regime (FY25–FY26): a beat is no longer enough. Jun 2025 −5% and Jun 2026 −13% both came on solid beats where the FY27 AI target was left unchanged.

spotSizing.reason: Derived from a 10% high-conviction base, trimmed for mega-cap upside magnitude. At $1.89T a beat moves the stock far less than a mid-cap, so the spot is sized for a smaller, lower-variance payoff.

breakdown.label: Base — high-conviction BUY (score 85, Fed risk LOW)
Pre-earnings run-up already partly captured in core

stopPreCatalyst.note: Break below $380 before earnings = below preferred entry zone, short-term thesis changes. Exit early.

stopPostCatalyst.note: Gap down >10% after earnings — exit within 30 min. As Jun 2026 (−13% on a beat) showed, the valuation premium makes re-rating fast and painful.
